lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: You're in my way. I have a route. The route has no kids in it.

lines.speaker: tadzio
lines.text: What's the bread for?

lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: For? It isn't FOR anything. It's yesterday's. Yesterday's bread goes back before morning, or morning gets confused.

lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: Two loaves in the cart already. One more on this street.

lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: ...Nobody ever asks.
You pick up the last loaf from a doorstep and carry it to the cart. It is heavier than bread should be.

lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: Careful. That one was a birthday.

lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: Now the list. I count, you check. One... two... I always lose count here.

lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: No. Count again. Two were in the cart. You carried one.

lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: Hey! I'm counting! Now I have to start over. One... two...

lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: Stop that! I'll lose my place! I ALWAYS lose my place!

lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: Three. Three loaves. All accounted for.

lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: You count good, for a kid off the list.
He tears the heel off a loaf and hands it to you.
You got a heel of bread.

lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: Forget it! I'll do the whole route backward!

lines.speaker: unbaker
lines.text: Tell the Foreman I'm owed a loaf.
The Un-Baker storms off, cart rattling.

lines.speaker: curfew
lines.text: Hush now... hush now... let's get you back to bed... high, low, and in between...

lines.speaker: tadzio
lines.text: When did you last sleep?

lines.speaker: curfew
lines.text: Sleep? Oh... I put everyone else to sleep. Every night. I'm always on shift.

lines.speaker: curfew
lines.text: I don't think I ever have.
You fluff the biggest pillow. It sighs.

lines.speaker: curfew
lines.text: Oh. Oh, that's nice. Nobody fluffs for me.

lines.speaker: curfew
lines.text: There's a song... I hum it to everyone... but I can't hum it to myself.

lines.speaker: curfew
lines.text: High notes fall on the right... low ones on the left... do you remember how it went?

lines.speaker: curfew
lines.text: Mmm... no... that's a different song. That one is for owls.
You pull the quilt up to Curfew's eyes and tuck in the edges. All the way around. It takes a while. It's a big quilt.

lines.speaker: curfew
lines.text: Now, now... that's not very sleepy of you.

lines.speaker: curfew
lines.text: Shhh... shhh... you'll wake the whole town.

lines.speaker: curfew
lines.text: Mmm... so this is what it's like...
Curfew yawns. It is an enormous yawn. The whole square yawns with it.

lines.speaker: curfew
lines.text: Fine... fine... I'm clocking out early.

lines.speaker: curfew
lines.text: Somebody else can tuck you in tonight.
